key_insight: Synchronising chaotic flow models by directly substituting observed variables is equivalent to a sliding mode observer, enabling stability analysis and robustness-oriented feedback design.
engineering_relevance: This framework supports principled state estimation for reduced-order turbulent flows despite chaotic amplification of prediction errors.
method: Interpret master–slave synchronisation as sliding mode observer design.
Seek Lyapunov stability certificates using parameter-dependent linear matrix inequalities and semidefinite programming.
Combine a neural ODE and decoder to learn mappings from observation histories to companion forms that simplify observer design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on the Lorenz system and a nine-dimensional reduced-order model of turbulent shear flow.
watch_item: Validation is limited to low-dimensional models; scalability and robustness to noisy measurements or model mismatch in full turbulent flows remain to be established.
paper_title: A sliding mode observer perspective on chaos synchronisation of turbulent flows
